eyebrow: Lesson 23 · B1 · Good Table Manners · 20 câu
heading: Mouthfuls and Fingers
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Good Table Manners – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 12–15.
credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Good Table Manners (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.

paras.label: A
paras.text: It is not polite to talk or {chomp|chomp} with your mouth full, and don't {stuff|stuff} too much food in at once. You can do all of that at a hot-dog eating {contest|contest}, but not at Grandma's table! Lift the food from your plate to your mouth; don't drop your face into your bowl. Leave that move for the dog!

paras.label: B
paras.text: If you need to leave the table to go to the toilet, put your napkin on your chair and say, "Please excuse me." And if you ever eat in China, don't finish everything on your plate. Your host may think you are rude, but leaving a little shows that you are a good guest.

paras.label: C
paras.text: Don't {slurp|slurp} your food or lick your fingers; nobody wants to listen to that! Never stick your finger in the cake {icing|icing}, however good it looks, and don't {double-dip|double-dip} your crisp in the dip. Nobody wants your {germs|germs}!

paras.label: D
paras.text: Only eat with your fingers when the food is meant to be eaten that way. Don't grab your pork chop like a {caveman|caveman}, but it's fine to pick up a taco. It also depends on where you are: in fancy restaurants, even chips are eaten with a fork.

paras.label: E
paras.text: Sometimes the rules are {turned upside down|turned upside down}. In Japan, slurping your noodle soup is a good thing, and the louder, the better! It tells the cook that you really enjoyed the meal.

vocab.vi: chấm lại lần hai (sau khi đã cắn)

parts.title: Part 1 · Matching headings
parts.instr: Chọn tiêu đề phù hợp cho mỗi đoạn. Mỗi tiêu đề dùng một lần.
options: Leaving the table – and leaving some food
A custom that breaks the rule

items.label: Paragraph A
items.why: Đoạn A: không nói khi miệng đầy, không cúi mặt vào bát.

items.label: Paragraph B
items.why: Đoạn B: xin phép rời bàn; ở Trung Quốc để lại chút thức ăn.

items.label: Paragraph C
items.why: Đoạn C: không húp, không liếm tay, không chấm lại – vi trùng.

items.label: Paragraph D
items.why: Đoạn D: món nào được ăn bằng tay.

items.label: Paragraph E
items.why: Đoạn E: ở Nhật, húp to lại là lịch sự.

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False.

questions.q: Where does the writer say stuffing your mouth might be OK?
questions.why: *You can do all of that at a hot-dog eating contest.*

questions.q: Before you leave the table, you should put your napkin on your chair.
questions.why: Đúng. *put your napkin on your chair and say, "Please excuse me."*

questions.q: Why should you leave a little food on your plate in China?
options: Finishing everything may seem rude to your host.
It shows that you are full of energy.
questions.why: *Your host may think you are rude…*

questions.q: Why is double-dipping a bad idea?
options: It makes the dip too salty.

questions.q: According to (D), you should always eat with a knife and fork.
questions.why: Sai. *it's fine to pick up a taco.*

questions.q: What is the main point of (E)?
options: Something rude in one place can be polite in another.
You should never eat noodle soup.
questions.why: Húp to: bất lịch sự ở nơi khác nhưng lịch sự ở Nhật.

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

questions.q: Which paragraph gives advice for the girl in this picture?
questions.why: Đoạn A: *don't drop your face into your bowl.*
questions.alt: An elderly woman eats soup with a spoon while a girl and a dog beside her lean down into their bowls

questions.q: Which sentence from the text is a joke about the animal in this picture?
options: Leave that move for the dog!
questions.why: Chú chó cúi mặt vào bát → *Leave that move for the dog!*
questions.alt: An elderly woman eats soup with a spoon while a girl and a dog beside her lean down into their bowls

questions.q: What should the girl NOT do after biting her crisp?
options: dip it into the bowl again
offer the bowl to her friend
questions.alt: Two girls share a bowl of crisps and dip; one dips a crisp into the bowl while the other watches

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn ngắn và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: Last summer my family went on holiday to Japan. [1] Everyone around us was slurping loudly. [2] So I tried it too, and the cook gave me a big smile. [3]
options: The waiter asked us to be quiet because slurping was rude.
On the first evening, we went to a small restaurant that served noodle soup.
At first, I was shocked, because at home slurping is bad manners.
We ate pizza with knives and forks at our hotel.
I learnt that good manners can be very different in different countries.

items.why: Phản ứng ban đầu với tiếng húp.

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của từ/cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh.

questions.q: *…talk or chomp with your mouth full* (A). To **chomp** means to…
*Don't grab your pork chop like a caveman* (D). This means don't eat it…
options: in a wild way with your hands

questions.q: *…don't double-dip your crisp* (C). To **double-dip** is to…
options: put food you have bitten back into a shared dip
questions.why: Chấm lại lần hai sau khi đã cắn.
